title: Urban Representation Learning for Identifying Potential Disparities in Crime Reporting
abstract: arXiv:2611.21825v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Open crime data support urban safety analysis but reflect reported incidents rather than the complete distribution of criminal activity, potentially introducing spatial distortions in downstream analysis. We propose a self-supervised urban representation learning framework for identifying unusual reporting patterns relative to representation-similar peers using only georeferenced crime records. The method constructs complementary hourly, weekly, and static reporting profiles, learns scale-specific representations under geographic self-supervision, and integrates them into a unified latent space. Neighbor Profile Divergence (NPD) is then used to quantify disagreement between each region's reporting profile and those of its retrieved peers. Experiments on more than 1.8 million crime records from Mexico City, aggregated into 1,058 H3 regions, show that the proposed representation achieves a mean Silhouette score of 0.4052, compared with 0.2

translated_title: 面向识别犯罪报告潜在差异的城市表征学习
translated_abstract: 开放犯罪数据能够支持城市安全分析，但它们反映的是已报告的案件而非犯罪活动的完整分布，这可能给下游分析带来空间扭曲。我们提出了一种自监督的城市表征学习框架，仅利用带地理坐标的犯罪记录来识别相对于表征相似同伴区域的异常报告模式。该方法构建了互补的小时级、周级和静态报告画像，在地理自监督下学习特定尺度的表征，并将其整合到统一的潜在空间中。随后，利用邻居画像差异指标来量化每个区域的报告画像与其检索到的同伴区域画像之间的不一致程度。在墨西哥城超过180万条犯罪记录（聚合为1,058个H3区域）上的实验表明，所提出的表征方法达到了0.4052的平均轮廓系数，相比之下为0.2...
tldr: 提出了一种自监督城市表征学习框架，通过邻居画像差异（NPD）指标量化各区域与其表征相似同伴区域的报告画像差异，从而识别开放犯罪数据中的潜在报告偏差。
en_tdlr: Proposes a self-supervised urban representation learning framework that uses Neighbor Profile Divergence (NPD) to quantify differences between each region's crime reporting profile and those of representation-similar peer regions, identifying potential reporting disparities in open crime data.
